title: Consumer-aware token accumulation and fair-share attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Current token aggregation jobs attribute per-customer usage by naively folding session windows and source tags. This produces unfair skew for multi-tenant routes where background worker tasks, retries, or bursty SDK clients allocate disproportionate tokens to a small subset of consumers. We need a consumer-aware accumulation job that enforces fairness across producers, supports late-arriving events, and provides deterministic attribution for billing and chargeback reports.

Goals:
- Produce a per-customer, per-route token accounting feed that is stable for billing windows and explains adjustments.
- Implement a fair-share algorithm that compensates for retries/spillover and reduces amplification from SDK batching mismatches.
- Be resilient to out-of-order events (up to 48 hours) and provide a compact corrections delta stream for downstream invoicing.
- Support both hosted and Dedicated routing metadata and emit provenance to the usage index for Console insights.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change pricing logic or rate-limits. It focuses on attribution and the post-aggregation correction stream.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Ingest canonical token events from the streaming gateway and enrich with route/tenant context using the existing usage-proxy materialized view.
2) Partition accumulation by customer+route+hour and maintain a lightweight per-partition sketch (count-min with sliding window) to detect producer skew.
3) Apply fair-share normalization: detect producer-dominant flows and redistribute a configurable fraction of spillover tokens proportionally across active producers in the same window.
4) Persist both the raw accumulation and the correction delta into the billing-attribution topic. Downstream jobs (invoicing/console metrics) can apply corrections idempotently.
5) Emit audit records (reason codes) for each correction so Console can show explainable adjustments.

Tradeoffs and considerations:
- Determinism vs. latency: strict determinism requires stronger ordering guarantees and state compaction which increases end-to-end latency. We will prioritize a bounded-latency mode (default) with optional deterministic compaction for month-end runs.
- Memory footprint: per-partition sketches save memory but introduce approximation errors; choose parameters to keep error <1% for top 99.9% of customers.
- Backfill handling: late-arriving events create correction deltas; we'll cap backfill windows at 48h and surface any longer tails to the billing ops queue.

Schema and contracts:
- billing-attribution topic messages: message_type ["raw_accum","correction_delta","audit_record"], tenant_id, route_id, window_start, window_end, token_count, correction_reason, upstream_event_ids (list). Messages must be compactable by (tenant_id,route_id,window_start).
- Console must be able to render correction_reason strings and link to upstream_event_ids (comma-separated).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for sketch and redistribution logic (deterministic inputs).
- Local integration harness using sample streaming gateway traces (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/consumer-aware-accum).
- Canary: enable job for 5% of customers (non-billing) and compare resulting invoice deltas against current pipeline for 7 days.
- Full rollout gated on <0.25% discrepancy in total tokens across all routes and manual sign-off from Billing Ops.

Observability:
- Expose per-partition memory usage, sketch error estimates, correction-rate, and percent of windows with spillover.
- Create a Console dashboard (billing-v2 > Attribution > FairShare) and a Grafana alert for correction_rate > 3% sustained over 1h.

Open questions:
- Edge-case semantics for multi-tenant shared endpoints: should certain system producers (e.g., internal health-checkers) be exempted? (pinged infra)
- Best encoding for upstream_event_ids to keep Kafka message size bounded.

Estimated effort and timeline:
- Design and proto: 3 days (Maya/Diego)
- Implementation (job + tests + schema evol): 2 weeks
- Canary and monitoring: 1 week

References and artifacts:
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Fair+Share+Token+Attribution
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/usage-pipeline/pull/1182
- Local harness and sample traces: gs://redwood-analytics/billing-v2/fairshare-samples/
- Billing ops runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fA-fairshare-runbook
